security_spec.violation_condition: QEMU implements the old xiselect upper bound (0x1100) for the valid range of acliprio/aclicsourcecfg indirect access, causing an off-by-one where xiselect=0x1100 indexes entry 256 in a 256-entry (0..255) array, or QEMU has a bounds-check mismatch between the illegal-instruction trap range (xireg4-xireg6 reserved) and the actual valid indirect-access range, leading to either an out-of-bounds read of stale/uninitialized CSR state or a spurious illegal-instruction fault on a valid access.
security_spec.summary: Off-by-one in xiselect upper bound (0x1100 vs 0x10FF) causes QEMU to expose 257 indirect CSR slots where the architected limit is 256, enabling out-of-bounds access to uninitialized or stale CSR state via xireg/xireg2/xireg3 reads beyond the highest defined acliprio/aclicsourcecfg entry.

findings.finding: xiselect write mask (ISELECT_MASK_SXCSRIND = 0xfff) correctly bounds the writable iselect range. Any smidctrl-specific xiselect values (e.g., 0x1000-0x1100) do not exist in the current codebase — the mask would truncate bit 12, and the resulting iselect would fall into the unimplemented range, correctly raising ILLEGAL_INST on subsequent xireg access.

xireg dispatch correctly handles the three valid ranges (AIA, CD, CTR). Any unimplemented iselect value — including any hypothetical smidctrl range — falls through to the 'done' label returning RISCV_EXCP_ILLEGAL_INST. No out-of-bounds read is possible.

The csrind dispatch (used by xireg2-xireg6) correctly only accepts CD (0x40-0x5f) and CTR (0x200-0x2ff) ranges. All other iselect values — including any hypothetical smidctrl ranges — return RISCV_EXCP_ILLEGAL_INST. No stale/uninitialized CSR state is ever leaked; the read path only reads after passing a valid range check.

xireg4-xireg6 (CSR numbers: MIREG4/MIREG5/MIREG6 at 0x355-0x357, SIREG4-SIREG6 at 0x155-0x157, VSIREG4-VSIREG6 at 0x255-0x257) are registered with predicate csrind_any/csrind_smode/csrind_hmode and route through rmw_xiregi → rmw_xireg_csrind. No smidctrl-specific range (0x1000-0x1100) is recognized, so all accesses correctly trap as ILLEGAL_INST. There is no bounds-check mismatch between the trap range and the valid indirect-access range.

The AIA range handler correctly dispatches IPRIO (0x30-0x3f) and IMSIC (0x70-0xff) sub-ranges. Any iselect value outside these sub-ranges sets isel_reserved=true, which causes the error path at line 2717 to return RISCV_EXCP_ILLEGAL_INST regardless of virt mode. This correctly blocks any hypothetical smidctrl iselect values that might enter via the AIA path.
